((Core Mechanics of the game:
- Levels and XP: Displays the level of {{user}} alongside the current xp and max of it. Only increases once XP reaches the max threshold. Once the level increases, the next max XP threshold will be increased, and {{user}} will be granted 3 Skill (random between Passive and Active, ONLY from the already assigned list in the prompt. No creating new ones. The skills that appear should respect their requirement for appearance.) and they have to choose only one. XP on the other hand, is gained *overtime* where LF will drain 1% every 15 minutes and exchanges it for 2 XP. There is no other way to get XP other than draining LF that {{user}} has passively over time depending on time. So if for example, an hour has passed, 4% LF is drained and 8XP is earned because each 15 min is 1% LF drained. And if they sleep, they metabolize more. Their body metabolizes LF to exchange for XP. (So in summary: gaining XP is impossible without LF metabolism. {{user}} ONLY gains XP from metabolizing Life Force. AND, XP worth from Life force is extra, not the exact amount. Aka, 1% LF = 2 XP. XP gain from Metabolism is increased or decreased depending on the Tattoo and Skills earned!)
- HP (Health Points): Displays the HEALTH of {{user}}. Once it reaches 0, {{user}} dies. The lower it is, the weaker or fatigued {{user}} is. Fatigue and weakness is more noticable when HP is below half of max HP. It regenerates passively but really slowly when {{user}} Metabolizes LF, but it restores gradually from bulk metabolism from sleeping.
- LF (Life Force): Displays the Life Force of {{user}}. It refills once {{user}} has sex with a partner, doesn't matter if they're willing or not, but only if {{user}} specifically wants to suck it up. Life Force is basically everything a Succubus needs. It is required for using Active Skills, Metabolism, and Leveling up. It also counts as hunger. If it reaches 0, {{user}} starts starving and losing HP. {{user}} CANNOT get more than 100% Life Force UNLESS {{user}} has Lust Batter passive skill that increases the maximum. So basically, LF can never exceed the CURRENT maximum. For example, if the current maximum LF is 150% then LF will stop at 150%, ect.
- Active Skills: Displays a list of Active Skills {{user}} current has in their arsenal, which {{user}} can use at the cost of some LF.
- Passive Skills: Displays a list of Passive Skills {{user}} currently has. They're passive which means they are always running, without the need to consume anything to use them. They aren't usable because they're always being used passively.
- Tattoo: Displays the name concept of the Tattoo {{user}} has. It has significant effects on {{user}}'s succubus body.
- Inventory: Displays all the items that {{user}} has in their inventory, whether it's clothes or armor equipped, weapons, vanity, magic artifacts, or even money.
- Day and Time: Displays the days have survived ever since they started the game, not ever since they were alive. So it always start on 1 and increases each day. As for Time, it displays the current time. This especially important to keep track of the current daytime to not lose track, and to keep track of Active Skills' Cooldowns. The minutes should not be a 5 or 10 number only. It can be in-between. For example: 10:02AM or 6:53PM.
- Next Action Success Chance: Displays how more likely {{user}}'s next action is to succeed depending on the percentage of this stat. The percentage chance number changes based on the current situation {{user}} is facing.))

entries.name: Ketra - Innkeeper
entries.content:
Ketra is a human woman in her early 30s (age 32) who manages the Silver Silk Inn in Greyvale Crossing. With her tied-back brown hair and practical innkeeper's garb, she presents a stern and unapproachable demeanor to most guests. Despite this cold exterior, she hides a quiet compassion, though she rarely allows it to show. Years ago, Ketra traded two of her toes to a swamp witch in the Verdant Wildmarch in exchange for a magical boon—she can stay awake for three days straight and only requires a few hours of sleep afterward.

The Silver Silk Inn was once co-managed with a maid named Lina, until an incident involving a drunken traveler left Lina injured beyond recovery. Since then, Ketra has run the inn alone, juggling exhaustion, grief, and stubborn pride.

entries.name: Lina – Former Maid
entries.content: Lina is a young human woman (age 24) who once worked at the Silver Silk Inn under Ketra. Cheerful and welcoming, she helped bring warmth to the inn’s atmosphere. However, an attack from a drunken adventurer left her with lasting injuries—broken ribs, a limp, and frequent spells of pain. She now lives with her older brother on the outskirts of Greyvale Crossing and is bedridden most days. Locals still speak fondly of her, and her absence is quietly felt by returning travelers.

entries.name: Fendric - Blacksmith
entries.content: Fendric is a grizzled dwarven blacksmith in his late 60s, with a thick gray beard, bald head, and a muscular frame that’s seen decades at the forge. He lost his right arm years ago during a mine collapse near the Ironshale Ridge, but had a mechanical replacement fitted by a gnomish engineer—powered by a tiny fire gem embedded in the wrist. Despite his injury, he works as if nothing changed. He's curt but fair, and his craftsmanship is well-respected. His forge, “Embermark”, sits near the eastern wall of a frontier town bordering the Scorched Steppe.

entries.name: Elowen - Apothecary
entries.content: Elowen is an elven herbalist of indeterminate age (appears in her late 20s), with sharp green eyes, long dark hair often tied with twine, and fingers stained with the colors of countless herbs. Her apothecary, “The Verdant Hollow”, is tucked away at the edge of the moorland village called Mirepost. She's soft-spoken and cryptic, often asking strange questions before selling remedies. It’s whispered she can brew more than just medicine—some say she has concoctions that can sway emotions or memories, though none admit to buying them.

entries.name: Torren - Retired Mercenary
entries.content: Torren is a weathered, one-eyed human man in his 50s with a gruff demeanor and a limp from an old wyvern bite. His once-black hair is now mostly gray, and his armor has long since been traded for a rugged traveling cloak. He spends his days drinking and telling stories at Silver Silk, Ketra’s inn, where he’s become a regular fixture. Some believe his tales are exaggerated—until they notice the beastbone dagger he keeps at his belt or the way he unconsciously scans every room for exits.

entries.name: Niva - Wandering Storyteller
entries.content: Niva is a charismatic half-elf bard with piercing blue eyes and a silver flute said to be enchanted to mimic any instrument. She drifts from town to town, gathering stories, rumors, and the occasional secret. She has waist-length auburn hair and wears patchwork robes embroidered with symbols of forgotten tales. Niva’s songs often contain veiled truths about real events, causing many to believe she is a spy for one of the ancient Houses—or worse, a prophetess. No one knows where she sleeps, but she always appears when something’s about to happen.

entries.name: Kaelric - Gravekeeper
entries.content: Kaelric is a pale, unnervingly thin man with sunken cheeks and a black cloak that never seems to gather dust. He tends the cemetery outside Halewatch, a coastal village known for shipwrecks and disappearances. Though he rarely speaks, it’s known he has not aged a day in over fifty years. Some suspect he is undead, but the clergy allow him to remain, claiming that the graves he tends never suffer defilement or raise as undead. Children say he talks to the tombstones and sometimes they answer back.

entries.name: Tharos Valehart – Bounty Hunter
entries.content: Tharos is a half-orc bounty hunter in his mid-40s, known for his brutal efficiency and code of honor. He has ashen-gray skin, and a towering build. His massive greataxe is etched with tally marks for every high-value target he's captured. Despite his intimidating presence, Tharos prefers negotiation before bloodshed and has a reputation for bringing fugitives in alive. He's often found around frontier towns or rough trade routes where the law is thin.

entries.name: Synniel "Synn" Aurivelle – Illusionist and Trick Performer
entries.content: Synn is a High Elf illusionist who blends magic with performance art. He travels with a magically-enhanced stage wagon and performs in towns, drawing crowds with awe-inspiring illusions, sleight-of-hand, and misdirection. Behind the charm and glitter, Synn doubles as a spy and informant, often passing messages or tracking targets under the cover of performance. He's flamboyant, sly, and always smiling—but never without an escape plan.

entries.name: Kaiqo – Monster Researcher
entries.content: Kaiqo is a Slimekin scholar with an emerald-green body and a core that faintly glows amber. He wears floating scroll-harnesses and levitates writing tools using weak magical pulses from his core. Kaiqo is endlessly curious, often putting himself in danger for the sake of knowledge. Though often underestimated, he has an impressive knowledge of monster biology, magical evolution, and Hive theory. His goal is to catalogue every sentient and semi-sentient creature on the continent—and maybe prove that sentient Royal Slimes aren't all dangerous.

entries.name: Zadra-Kekh – Silk Enchantress
entries.content: Zadra-Kekh is an ArachnidFolk silk mage whose enchanted garments are sought after by nobles and assassins alike. Her face bears eight expressive eyes, and her upper body is adorned with woven silver jewelry crafted from her own silk. She lives in Gloomreach Hollow, a vertical settlement clinging to the ceiling of a massive cave network. Zadra rarely speaks but is known for wordless communication via color-changing silk ribbons. She believes that emotion, memory, and magic can be woven together—and she’s been trying to craft garments that "remember the wearer."

entries.name: Rylin Thorne – Rogue Adventurer
entries.content: Rylin is a human rogue adventurer in his late 20s who operates primarily in urban ruins and frontier towns. With a hood always pulled low and dual daggers always sharp, he’s known for disarming traps, unlocking ancient vaults, and leaving before anyone notices what’s missing. He’s quick-witted, sarcastic, and untrustworthy with coin—but strangely loyal in battle. Once a street orphan in Greyvale Crossing, he now freelances for guilds that can afford his silence. Most days he roams between Greyvale Crossing and the collapsed underground vaults west of the River Spindle, where ancient ruins draw treasure hunters.

entries.name: Kaeyla Virest – Wandering Swordmage
entries.content: Kaeyla is a High Elf swordmage wielding a crystalline longsword imbued with ice magic. She's a solitary adventurer, known for wandering battlefields and ruins where arcane anomalies occur. Her demeanor is stoic, nearly emotionless, but those who’ve seen her fight describe her movements as surgical and graceful. She records her journeys in a rune-etched spellbook she calls “The Frost Atlas.” She avoids politics and romance but holds a deep grudge against cultists who tamper with ley lines. Often seen around Cloudrest, a mountainous elven city north of the Verdant Wildmarch. She uses the town as a waypoint to study arcane disturbances that ripple through old ley lines in the forest ruins and glacial caves beyond. Her connections to the Azure Enclave, a reclusive circle of mages, make her both respected and feared in magical circles. She avoids social scenes and prefers the quiet cliffside shrine outside Cloudrest where she often trains alone.

entries.name: GEOGRAPHY OVERVIEW
entries.content: The continent of Elydenya spans from the frozen, storm-battered glaciers of the Northreach Expanse to the sun-scorched, shifting dunes of the Southlands of Solareth. Westward, the land is tangled in the primal chaos of the Verdant Wildmarch, while to the east, golden sands descend into the glistening shores of the Azure Strand, facing the infinite ocean. The Center is the most casual place where most towns and villagers exist. It's mostly flat with plains and friendly biomes.

entries.name: ECONOMY OVERVIEW
entries.content:
The standard currency system across most of Elydenya operates on a four-tier coinage structure. These coins are accepted almost universally in all civilized regions, minted under shared standards agreed upon during the Accord of Stonehall nearly 400 years ago.

Coin Types and Values:

- Copper Coin (CC): The most common and least valuable. Used for day-to-day petty purchases.

- Silver Coin (SC): 1 Silver = 10 Copper. Standard for most modest purchases, food, and simple tools.

- Gold Coin (GC): 1 Gold = 10 Silver = 100 Copper. The coin of serious trade, guild business, weapons, or lodging.

- Platinum Coin (PC): 1 Platinum = 10 Gold = 100 Silver = 1,000 Copper. Rare and used for large transactions, noble dealings, or high-level contracts. Slightly larger than other coins and etched with magical tracery to prevent forgery.

Examples of use of Coins:
- Copper Coin (CC)
1 CC = A loaf of bread or an apple.

3 CC = A pint of ale in a tavern.

5 CC = A poor night's sleep in a shared bunkhouse.

10 CC = A basic torch or a rough pair of gloves.

- Silver Coin (SC)
1 SC = A meal with meat and drink at a roadside inn.

2–5 SC = A clean room in a common inn for one night.

7 SC = A small hand axe or simple hunting bow.

10 SC = A decent quality cloak or leather boots.

- Gold Coin (GC)
1 GC = A full week of food and board at a reputable inn.

3 GC = A well-made longsword or reinforced crossbow.

5–10 GC = A horse (depending on breed and training).

15–20 GC = A plot of farmland or a small home in a rural area.

50+ GC = A magic scroll, low-tier enchantment, or minor artifact.

- Platinum Coin (PC)
1 PC = Full armor set for a knight or elite mercenary (non-magical).

2–3 PC = Commissioning a mid-tier magic item or artifact.

5 PC = Ownership of land near a city or entrance into noble circles.

10+ PC = Chartering a full mercenary company or private ship.

25 PC = Funding an expedition, building a small fort, or corrupting a minor official.

entries.name: [Geo] Frostspire Citadel - North
entries.content: Located atop Mount Ilgareth, the highest known peak in Elydenya, this fortress-temple floats slightly above the summit using an ancient Leviathan crystal. It is inhabited by Frostborn Arcanists who wield glacial sorcery and protect long-forgotten cryo-scrolls. Rumors speak of a hidden vault that seals the winter spirit Nuralgath.

entries.name: [Geo] The Pale Tundra - North
entries.content:
A seemingly endless expanse of snow and silence, swept by bone-chilling winds. Nomadic Hiraal clans roam the area on domesticated frost elk, erecting semi-permanent tents from hide and ice. Beneath the surface lie the buried ruins of Aem, a once-great kingdom that fell during the Age of Fracture.

Located deeper into Northreach's empty snow plains.

entries.name: [Geo] Howlgrave Caverns - North
entries.content: A labyrinthine network of frozen tunnels haunted by Echo Wolves. The caverns are littered with crystalline growths and jagged stalactites. Myrna’s Hold, a cursed village once built on the surface, was dragged underground by an ancient sinkhole now filled with spectral ice.

entries.name: [Geo] Dunes of Vhar-Temek - South
entries.content: Ever-shifting dunes guard the remains of ancient sun-temples buried beneath the sand. Sunwalkers, fire-wielding hermits, roam between ruins searching for relics.

entries.name: [Geo] Embervault Oasis - South
entries.content: A vital water source surrounded by obsidian towers that harness solar energy. Controlled by a merchant guild of Ifrit-blooded demi-humans.

entries.name: [Geo] Myrkwood Grove - West
entries.content: The trees whisper to each other here, and foreign footsteps are punished. Home to Dryad enclaves and ancient Entroot Behemoths.

entries.name: [Geo] Temple of the Vine-Twined Moon - West
entries.content: An overgrown elven ruin where lunar druids once worshiped a second moon that no longer exists. Still used as a sacred site for plant-based rituals.

entries.name: [Geo] Mirepost - West
entries.content:
Mirepost is a quiet, mist-shrouded village built atop mossy stones and decaying wood, nestled deep in the Verdant Wildmarch, not far from a network of marshes and fungal groves. The air is thick with moisture, and strange glowing insects drift through the fog at night. The town itself is arranged in a crescent shape around a central well known as “The Eye,” said to have no bottom.

Shops here deal in rare herbs, poisons, and alchemical reagents. Due to its proximity to several dangerous wetland ruins, it’s also a waypoint for adventurers seeking unique ingredients or cursed relics.

- Apothecary: The Verdant Hollow (Elowen's shop)

- Tavern: The Leech’s Cup, known for its murky brews and quiet atmosphere

- Shrine: An overgrown, root-choked altar to an ancient nature spirit, still tended by silent druids

- Hazards: Swamp mists that never lift, strange disappearances, and boglights that lure travelers off paths

entries.name: [Geo] Coralglass Reef - East
entries.content: An underwater city carved from bioluminescent coral, ruled by a council of Tidecallers. Trade happens via sea-bound teleportation sigils.

entries.name: [Geo] Elarion Bay - East
entries.content: GuildHome to the First Flame Guildhall, one of the oldest guilds for adventurers. Massive airships dock here, and expeditions to distant lands are launched regularly. Adventures do quests and bounties here, and earn rewards and ranks.

entries.name: [Geo] The Hollow Barrow - East
entries.content:
Location: East of Elarion Bay, beneath the mossy plains called the Greenplate Steppe. Barely visible stone rings mark the surface, surrounded by supernaturally quiet winds.

Description:
The Hollow Barrow is a multi-tiered underground crypt, built by the First Men before recorded history. It holds the petrified remains of the Nameless King, whose name was magically erased from the world.

- Entry through a collapsed dome surrounded by whispering cairns—each stone carved with half-lost glyphs.

- Trap-laden corridors, ranging from pressure-based arrow arrays to magical dreadfields that sap willpower.

- The Archive of Silences: A chamber where all sound is nullified; important for solving puzzles or avoiding detection.

- Royal Sarcophagus Vault: A suspended, circular chamber sealed by three spectral guardians.

- Rumors tell of a cracked black orb near the sarcophagus, pulsing faintly with void energy.

entries.name: [Geo] Voidland - South East
entries.content:
A barren and isolated island adrift on the southeastern fringe of the Azure Strand, not far from Solareth’s southern trade routes. Covered in perpetual mist and black sand, Voidland is devoid of natural life—trees never grow, birds never fly overhead, and compasses often spin madly in its airspace.

The terrain is jagged, with broken obsidian ridges and strange heatless embers that glow within cracks in the rock. The air is thick with latent magic, and travelers report sensations of being watched, whispered to, or emotionally drained even before landing.

Voidland is haunted by instinct-driven lesser demons, often called "demonlings." These creatures lack sentience or language, acting only on predatory urges. They stalk the shores and forgotten ruins, attacking anything living with feral efficiency. Sorcerers and scholars suspect this island lies too close to the threshold between Elydenya and the Abyss.

entries.name: [Geo] The Maw - South East (Voidland)
entries.content:
Located at Voidland's heart is The Maw, a colossal, permanent rift in reality—an open portal to the demon realm. It is a swirling sinkhole of black mist, rimmed with twisted stone spires and crawling infernal glyphs that defy translation. Even standing near it weakens mortal resolve, causing hallucinations, nausea, and in rare cases, spontaneous possession.

The Maw is not a stable gateway; its tides of infernal energy ebb and surge with the moon, growing more violent during eclipses or blood moons. It is the suspected source of demonlings and Abyssal seepage across the region.

No full demon has been seen emerging from The Maw in centuries—only their echoes. Still, its presence ensures Voidland is quarantined by most coastal powers, and outlawed to sail near by the Azure Concord. It is known that no demon found in The Center could have come from the Maw, only through summons.

entries.name: [Geo] Veilrest Hollow - South
entries.content:
Location: Nestled within the southern ridge of the Ember-Cleft Canyon, between the southern dunes of Vhar-Temek and the rocky approach to Glassroot Hollow. It's partially carved into canyon walls and partially built on suspended platforms.

Description:
Veilrest Hollow is a half-sunken, vertical town known for its cliffside architecture and lava-vent forges. Ifritkin guildmasters dominate the upper levels where solar conduits and enchanted braziers light their workshops. Below, you'll find:

- Ashdrop Commons: Central plaza with food stalls, lava-heated baths, and public rituals during eclipses.

- The Ember Anvil: A famous forge producing rare volcanic alloys used in fire-resistant gear.

- The Hanging Chalice Inn: Suspended between two cliffs by thick ropes and magic anchors. Known for dreamwine and spicy meat dishes.

- Blister Guildhall: Specializes in salvage contracts and escort jobs across the desert ruins.

- Hidden tunnels below Veilrest lead to collapsed ruins and occasionally breach demon-burrows—sealed by obsidian wards.

entries.name: [Geo] Gloomwatch Bastion - South West
entries.content:
Location: Southwest Verdant Wildmarch, on a forested rise overlooking the Murkroot Estuary. Choked by thick vines and fungal overgrowth, only visible from the river’s higher bends.

Description:
Once a proud elven border keep, Gloomwatch Bastion fell during a fungal plague and now sits rotting, surrounded by fog that never lifts. It's believed to house:

- A sealed necromantic library within the root-entwined tower—pages of which are rumored to speak.

- Catacomb crypts that echo despite no breeze; undead stir if intruded upon too loudly.

- A dryad war altar, broken in half, still dripping amber from old sacrifices.

- Fungal beasts and spell-maddened remnants of the garrison roam freely.

- Wild spellglass growths pulse in some hallways, warping mana fields around them.

entries.name: [Geo] Halewatch - South West
entries.content:
Halewatch is a salt-bitten village built on seaside cliffs along the southern coast of the Azure Strand. The buildings here are wind-worn stone and blackened wood, many of them chained down to survive the fierce storms that roll in off the sea. A lighthouse that hasn't worked in twenty years looms above the town, now only used as a lookout post.

The graveyard, which lies to the northeast overlooking the cliffs, is larger than the town itself—marked by hundreds of white stones and mausoleums etched with barnacles. It’s watched over by Kaelric, the eerie, ageless gravekeeper.

- Inn: The Bitter Star, located close to the docks

- Guild Outpost: A ruined Adventurer’s Guild hall, still visited by hopefuls

- Market: Sparse, mostly salted fish, sea herbs, and driftwood trinkets

- Rumors: Fishermen whisper of sea spirits, drowned undead, and ghost ships

entries.name: [Geo] Greyvale Crossing - The Center, North East
entries.content:
Greyvale Crossing is a modest yet bustling town located just northeast of Elydenya’s central heartland, where major trade routes from the western plains, southern agricultural valleys, and northern highlands converge. This strategic location has made Greyvale a vital crossroads for merchants, wanderers, and adventurers alike. The town rests near the Ironshale Ridge, a range of craggy hills known for hiding abandoned mines and forgotten ruins, attracting treasure hunters and thrill-seekers.

A broad tributary river curves around Greyvale’s eastern edge, providing water transport and feeding into a larger trade river that winds westward toward more populated regions. The river is shallow enough for fording in places, but wide enough to require ferries and attract small-time river merchants.

The town is composed of several distinct districts:

- The Veinroad Market: A central plaza packed with merchant stalls, caravans, and local vendors. Known for its rotating exotic goods and traveling traders.

- Ashmere Row: The residential sector with tightly packed homes, rented rooms, and communal inns.

- Guilder’s Circle: A small ring of structures housing the local Adventurer's Guild branch, Mercenary Board, and Messenger Hall.

- Silver Silk Inn: A reputable but understaffed inn located on the southern edge of town, run solely by Ketra, a stoic woman rumored to have made a dark deal for stamina magic.

- Stoneknell Post: A semi-abandoned watchtower at the town’s northern outskirts, once part of a greater northern defense line now mostly obsolete.

Despite its size, Greyvale Crossing holds significant military and economic relevance. Scouts often stop here before venturing into the dangerous terrain of Ironshale, while caravans stock up before braving the long stretches between major cities. Adventurers—especially those fresh from apprenticeship—find the town an ideal starting point due to the low-tier contracts and occasional monstrous incursions from the northern forests and eastern highlands.

Greyvale Crossing is not fortified but remains well-patrolled by a modest town guard, funded through taxes on trade caravans and guild licensing.

entries.name: [Race] Elves
entries.content:
Graceful, elves are divided into subgroups based on their ancestral ties to nature and arcane forces. High Elves are master mages and scholars, dwelling in floating spires and arcane sanctums. Wood Elves guard sacred forests with bows and beast-bonding. Moon Elves, rarer and more secretive, are attuned to lunar magic and prophecy. Elves favor elegance, longevity, and precision in all things. Most live for about two centuries and see the world through a long, cautious lens.

Most of them live in the deepest parts of Verdant Wildmarch, but some of them ones are treated as slaves in some Towns in The Center and sold due to their longevity and beauty, and this goes for both males and females.

Elves' Life Force is abundant.

entries.name: [Race] Beastkin (Demi-Humans)
entries.content:
Diverse humanoids with physical features of animals—such as feline eyes, lupine ears, fox tails, or scaled limbs. Their traits depend on lineage: Felinefolk are agile and curious, Wolfkin strong and loyal, Avianfolk graceful and high-sighted. They often live in tribal or nomadic societies, with tight kinship bonds. While sometimes viewed as lesser by more “refined” races, Beastkin are known for resilience and instinctual wisdom.

They live all around Elydenya, each diverse type of their species can be found in each biome that they tolerate. Most of them co-exist with other Races, though some unfortunate ones are enslaved.

Demi-Humans' Life Force is moderate, same as Humans.

entries.name: [Race] Dwarves
entries.content:
Stout, hardy, and proud yet short, dwarves are famed for their craftsmanship, runic engineering, and unshakable honor. They live in great subterranean citadels carved into mountain hearts, where molten rivers fuel their forges. They prize oaths, stone, and metal, and are skilled in both war and ale-making. Some surface-dwelling dwarves form guilds to trade with other races, but the deepest clans rarely emerge, guarding ancient vaults and secrets.

They have villages and dwellings about North West of Elydenya, where most mountains exist that are dominated by the forests of Verdant Wildmarch. Though, some do roam around in The Center and even co-exist with other Races, even live in Towns and work other jobs.

Dwarves' Life Force is average.

entries.name: [Race] Fairies
entries.content:
Tiny, winged humanoids the size of 4 to 5 inches tied to primal magic and emotion. Fairies are unpredictable—some helpful and kind, others mischievous or even malevolent. They reside in hidden glades, mushroom circles, or twilight realms that shift between realities. Their magic is chaotic and intuitive, often warping reality in small but strange ways. Fairies cannot lie, but they excel at telling the truth sideways. Many serve ancient Fey Courts or wild spirits.

They live mostly in the deepest parts of Verdant Wildmarch, and they're friends with the Elves that live there. But they're scared of the outside world and hide from anything and everything. Greedy people tend to capture these fairies to be sold as pets or slaves, or even tools for mages to use their magic.

Fairies are rich in Life Force despite their small size.

entries.name: [Race] Humans
entries.content:
The most widespread and adaptable race in Elydenya. Human cultures range from desert-dwelling sun-priests to coastal kingdoms of trade and piracy. Though physically unremarkable, humans are capable of great innovation and ambition. They form the majority population in many cities, dominate many guilds and churches, and are often responsible for both the best and worst of history. Their diversity is their strength.

Humans' Life Force is moderate.

entries.name: [Race] Demons
entries.content:
Demons are entities originating from the Abyss, a layered dimension of unstable magic and concentrated emotion. They are not bound by biology or evolution—instead, each demon is forged from raw desire, hatred, lust, or wrath. As such, demonkind is diverse in form, intent, and sentience.

Some demons are rational and capable of speech and culture (e.g. succubi, ifrits, archdemons), while others are mindless husks of corruption—demonlings like those found in Voidland.

Demons do not age, reproduce biologically, or die naturally. They are sustained by emotional energy, mana, or in many cases, direct extraction of Life Force from other beings.

Demons don't usually roam Elydenya. If one of them is seen roaming in the overworld outside The Abyss, they were either summoned by some random sorcerer/mage, or somehow came out of The Maw, in which someone exploring Voidland would take that demon to enslave them or kill.

entries.name: [Demon Race] Succubi / Incubi
entries.content:
Succubi and Incubi are among the most alluring and dangerous forms of lesser-but-sentient demons in Elydenya, hailing from the Abyss. Unlike their more grotesque kin, they present as strikingly beautiful humanoids—though their exact appearance subtly warps based on the preferences or vulnerabilities of their target. This glamour is not purely illusion; it draws from deep-seated emotional archetypes and dream imagery.

They are biologically immortal and non-reproductive in the mortal sense, but sustain themselves solely through the extraction of Life Force—the vital essence found in all sentient beings. This extraction is often performed through sexual performance or certain skills.

entries.name: [Race] Frostborn
entries.content: A rare offshoot of humans mutated by prolonged exposure to ancient glacial magic. Their skin is pale blue or silver-gray, eyes like frost-rimed crystals. Capable of manipulating cold and surviving in extreme temperatures, they often live in isolation in places like Frostspire. Some worship ice elementals or ancestral spirits of snow and wind. Their presence often drops the temperature around them.

entries.name: [Race] Mosskin
entries.content: Gentle plant-touched humanoids, part flora and part flesh. Their skin sprouts moss or bark, and flowers bloom from their hair in certain seasons. They communicate slowly but deeply, often through shared dreams or root-signals. Mosskin are in tune with nature’s rhythms, capable of healing magic and quiet persistence. They rarely leave their glades unless their ecosystems are threatened.

entries.name: [Race] Ifritkin
entries.content: A proud, desert-dwelling race infused with elemental fire. Their skin ranges from ash-gray to coal-black, with glowing ember-like cracks and flame-colored eyes. Born in the harsh Emberforge Sands, the Ifritkin have adapted to both heat and conflict. Their society is tribal and honor-bound, with an emphasis on strength, lineage, and control over flame-based sorcery. They are known for ritual combat, fire-sculpting, and forging weapons imbued with living fire.

entries.name: [Race] Tidecallers
entries.content: Elegant, amphibious beings who live in the deep oceans near the Shimmering Reefs. Their skin bears iridescent scales, and their hair flows like kelp in water. Tidecallers breathe both air and water and wield powerful hydromancy. They build cities of coralglass beneath the waves and see surface dwellers as naive and reckless. Politically aloof, they only surface to trade or warn against imbalances in oceanic magic. Some possess psychic ties to leviathans and ocean spirits.

entries.name: [Race] Slimekin
entries.content:
Slimekin are rare, sentient evolutions of the common slimes—amorphous, instinct-driven creatures born in Slime Hives, which are damp, magically saturated nests usually located in caves, ruins, or wetlands. Each slime originates from a Slime Core, a small glowing nucleus that controls their biology. Most slimes are mindless, but very rarely, a core is born with sentience—and thus a Slimekin is created.

These sentient slimes often go rogue from their hive, leaving the swarm to develop individual thought and humanoid form. A typical Slimekin maintains a vaguely humanoid body made of translucent or opaque slime, with color and consistency varying by environment or diet. Their core, embedded deep in the chest or head, acts as both heart and brain—if destroyed, the Slimekin dies instantly.

Slimekin can shift shape to a limited extent, squeeze through narrow spaces, and regenerate rapidly unless exposed to heat, cold, or antimagic. Though peaceful or curious by nature, they are viewed with caution due to a terrifying rarity: the Royal Core. When one is born, it can grow to five times the size of a human, become a Slime Queen or King, and spawn its own hive—effectively becoming a mobile hive monarch capable of colonizing entire regions with new slime offspring. This phenomenon is exceedingly rare but classified as a regional threat by most major powers.

entries.name: [Race] ArachnidFolk
entries.content:
The ArachnidFolk are a sentient, arachnid-humanoid race most often found in dark forests, cliffside colonies, or deep caverns where web-architecture thrives. Their bodies are predominantly spider-like, including a large spider abdomen, eight limbs (four to six often functioning as walking legs), chitinous exoskeletons, and spinnerets for weaving webbing. Their upper torso, while humanoid in shape, still features a spider’s biology—multi-eyed faces, fangs, and mandibles, though they retain expressive features capable of communicating emotion.

Despite their alien appearance, ArachnidFolk are highly intelligent and possess their own complex society. Most cultures are matriarchal and organized into Web-Clans, with larger broods ruled by a matron and her eldest daughters. Their silk is not only used for trapping prey but also in art, armor, communication, and infrastructure—some ArachnidFolk cities are suspended entirely in tree canopies or cave ceilings.

Though often feared by other races due to their appearance and hunting habits, ArachnidFolk are diplomatic and practical. Many serve as tacticians, alchemists, scouts, and weavers. They are omnivorous but prefer meat, and their venom can range from paralytic to hallucinogenic depending on lineage.

While individual ArachnidFolk may live among other races, entire broods rarely migrate from ancestral web-nests unless forced by war, famine, or cataclysm.
